entities.summary: Andrea Doria, Prince of Melfi, was a pivotal Italian statesman, condottiero, and admiral who played a crucial role in the Republic of Genoa during his lifetime. Born around 1466 in the Republic of Genoa, Doria rose to prominence as a naval commander, capturing several key cities and territories that expanded Genoa's influence in the Mediterranean. His most notable achievement was the capture of the city of Lepanto in 1571, a victory that showcased his military prowess and secured Genoa's position as a dominant maritime power. Doria's legacy extends beyond his military victories, as he also implemented various reforms and infrastructure projects that modernized Genoa's government and economy. His impact can be seen in the subsequent rise of the House of Grimaldi, which would go on to rule Monaco for centuries. As the first Prince of Melfi, Doria's title reflected his status as a leader of the Genoese people, and his influence can still be felt in the modern-day Republic of San Marino, which declared independence from Genoa in 301 AD. Doria's story serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Republic of Genoa, a beacon of maritime power and cultural exchange that continues to inspire historians and enthusiasts alike. The 'Doria Code', a set of principles guiding naval warfare, remains in use to this day, a lasting testament to his strategic genius.
